answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Rounds. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge within one round; honest agents derive answers from private state that evolves via local inputs (a comet observation, a yarrow specimen, a horizon reading). Clones share identical state, so they produce identical answers, which the protocol flags as a collision. To pass, an attacker must maintain and synchronize divergent private state per identity, paying storage and update costs that scale linearly with clone count.
